title: Grammar: More than one: the plural
subtitle: Unit 3: Forms and papers

steps.title: More than one: the plural
steps.body: To make a plural, add -s to the noun and change the article: le passeport → les passeports, une rue → des rues. The s is silent, so you hear the plural only in the article: le → les (lay), un/une → des (day).

steps.title: More than one: the plural
steps.body:
• -eau → -eaux: le bureau → les bureaux.
• -al → -aux: le journal → les journaux.
• Words already ending in -s, -x, -z do not change: le pays → les pays.
• Before a vowel, les / des link with a z: les adresses (lay-zah-DREHS).

steps.title: In Canada
steps.body: On forms and in official French you see the masculine as the default. Canadian offices increasingly write both: Né(e) le, Canadien(ne). The (e) tells you to add an e if you are a woman.
